record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.context_brief: Gutzwiller trace formula beyond Ehrenfest time
record.original_question: For chaotic quantum systems, can the Gutzwiller trace formula and related semiclassical propagator approximations be justified for times substantially larger than the Ehrenfest time T_E ≈ log(λ)/χ_Lya, and in particular on time scales relevant for sharp spectral statistics? The problem asks how to control the quantum evolution after exponential separation of classical trajectories causes the usual semiclassical approximation to break down.

evidence.quote: The rule of the game is: the further in time you control the propagator, the more precise your spectral estimate becomes.

For a chaotic system, trajectories separate from each other at an exponential rate, which results in a breakdown of semiclassical approximations around the Ehrenfest time TE ≈ log λ / χ Lya, where χ Lya is the largest Lyapunov exponent.
In that view, a present line of investigation consists in trying to extend the validity of the Gutzwiller approximation to larger times [11].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold whose geodesic flow on the unit cotangent bundle is uniformly hyperbolic (Anosov), with largest Lyapunov exponent $\chi_{\mathrm{Lya}}>0$. Let $\hat H = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2}\Delta_g$ (or, more generally, an $\hbar$-pseudodifferential operator whose principal symbol generates such a chaotic Hamiltonian flow on a compact energy shell), and let $U(t)=e^{-it\hat H/\hbar}$ be the corresponding quantum propagator. The Gutzwiller trace formula is the semiclassical asymptotic expansion, as $\hbar\to 0$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}\!\bigl(\chi(\hat H)\,U(t)\bigr) \;\sim\; \sum_{\gamma\,:\,T_\gamma=t}\frac{T_\gamma^{\#}\,e^{i S_\gamma/\hbar - i\pi\mu_\gamma/2}}{\bigl|\det(I-P_\gamma)\bigr|^{1/2}},$$
summed over closed orbits $\gamma$ of period $t$ on the energy shell, with $S_\gamma$ the classical action, $\mu_\gamma$ the Maslov index, and $P_\gamma$ the linearized Poincaré map. The Ehrenfest time is $T_E(\hbar)=\dfrac{|\log\hbar|}{\chi_{\mathrm{Lya}}}$.

Determine whether the Gutzwiller trace formula, and the underlying semiclassical approximations to $U(t)$ used to derive it, can be rigorously justified — with controlled error as $\hbar\to 0$ — for times $t=t(\hbar)$ that grow substantially faster than $T_E(\hbar)$, in particular up to the time scales (such as the Heisenberg time $T_H \sim \hbar^{-(d-1)}$ on a $d$-dimensional manifold) needed to resolve fine spectral statistics of $\hat H$. Equivalently: identify the longest time scale $t(\hbar)$ on which one can prove a uniform semiclassical approximation for $U(t)$ on chaotic systems, going beyond the exponential separation of classical trajectories that breaks down the standard WKB/stationary-phase derivation at $t \sim T_E(\hbar)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists. Faure (Ann. Inst. Fourier, 2007; arXiv:nlin/0610004) extended the Gutzwiller-type trace formula beyond the Ehrenfest time for certain hyperbolic models using semiclassical normal forms, and subsequent work (e.g., Anantharaman–Nonnenmacher, Faure–Tsujii on Ruelle resonances, and recent encounter-calculus / many-body quantum chaos surveys such as Richter et al. 2022) has pushed semiclassical control past $T_E$ in specific settings. However, a rigorous justification up to the Heisenberg time relevant for sharp spectral statistics on general chaotic systems remains open.

status_evidence.title: Semi-classical formula beyond the Ehrenfest time in quantum chaos. (I) Trace formula
status_evidence.snippet: Extends a Gutzwiller-type trace formula beyond the Ehrenfest time using semiclassical normal forms for hyperbolic dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extension of the trace formula beyond T_E has been rigorously established in specific hyperbolic settings.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical roots of universality in many-body quantum chaos (Richter et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses encounter calculus and treatment of phenomena at and beyond Ehrenfest time scales based on Gutzwiller's trace formula.
status_evidence.claim: Active research extends semiclassical periodic-orbit methods beyond T_E, but full justification to Heisenberg time is not established in general.

status_evidence.title: A Periodic Orbit Trace Formula for Quantum Scrambling
status_evidence.snippet: Develops a periodic-orbit trace formula relevant to dynamics at and beyond the Ehrenfest time.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing work continues to push trace-formula validity past T_E.
